column2: # Reprovision a TrueNAS-hosted VM worker end-to-end, unattended:
#   1. configure_vms.yaml recreates THIS worker's VM with a blank zvol
#      (scoped via truenas_vms_only; other absent VMs are not recreated)
#   2. generate a full add-node ISO (`oc adm node-image create`, no
#   3. copy the ISO to the TrueNAS host, attach/refresh it as the VM's
#      CDROM (order 1005) and demote the netboot RAW below it for the
#      install boot, then start the VM
#   4. approve this node's CSRs (scoped, incl. decoding bootstrapper CSR
#      subjects) until the node is Ready, then restore the netboot RAW
# rebuild) lets this playbook sit in the linear
#   destroy — every play here no-ops (teardown already happened)
#   create  — reconcile: if the worker is already a Ready cluster node
#             the run ends green without touching it; otherwise it is
#             so an existing VM is left untouched either way)
#   rebuild — full reprovision; the node must be absent (asserted)
# E2E tested via AAP 2026-07-31 (3 rebuild cycles).
# Boot design — no netboot-pin changes required: with the zvol blank,
# the install boot falls through disk(1001, blank) -> agent ISO CDROM
# (1005; the netboot RAW is temporarily demoted to 1006 so the install
# never depends on firmware advancing past a failed iPXE exit), RHCOS
# installs and reboots, and the installed disk then boots first forever
# after. After the node joins, the netboot RAW is restored to 1004.
# The stale ISO stays attached but is NOT a usable reinstall path (its
# embedded ignition token expires within ~24h) — to rebuild again,
# - In rebuild mode the node must NOT currently exist in the cluster
# - No CSI smoke test here by design — validate storage manually once
- name: Validate vm_worker_state before touching anything
vm_worker_state must be create, rebuild or destroy
- name: Recreate the VM with a blank zvol (create-only, scoped to this worker)
# Full-ISO mode: suppress the PXE-only bootArtifactsBaseURL field in
- name: End play — vm_worker_state=destroy has nothing to provision
- name: Assert KUBECONFIG is set in the environment
fail_msg: Export KUBECONFIG before running this playbook.
- name: Discover nodes already joined to the cluster
# Persisted as a fact (not task vars) so the later truenas-hosted
- name: Record whether the worker is already a cluster node
- name: Assert the worker is not currently a cluster node (rebuild mode)
{{ worker }} is still a node in the cluster — run
- name: End play — create mode and the worker is already joined (no-op)
- name: Restrict nodes-config rendering to this worker
- name: Fetch cluster pull secret to work dir
- name: Lock down pull secret file mode
- name: Run `oc adm node-image create` (full ISO)
- name: Set fact for later plays — ISO path
- name: Attach the ISO and boot the VM
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Resolve the VM definition for this worker
- name: Assert the worker maps to a truenas_vms entry
No truenas_vms entry has openshift_node == {{ worker }} —
- name: Query the VM (created by the configure_vms import)
- name: Assert the VM exists and is stopped
VM {{ _vm_def.name }} is missing or not STOPPED — expected a
- name: Copy the add-node ISO to the host
# Query the VM's devices unfiltered and pick out dtypes client-side:
# `attributes.dtype` is a path into a JSON column, and middleware
# filter support for that is unverified — an ignored filter would
# return ALL devices and a blind `first` would then rewrite the boot
# disk or NIC. Jinja-side filtering is correct regardless.
- name: Index the VM's CDROM and netboot RAW devices
- name: Attach the ISO as a new CDROM (order 1005)
- name: Point the existing CDROM at the fresh ISO
# Whether UEFI advances to the next boot entry when the netboot
# image's iPXE exits non-zero is firmware-dependent; don't bet the
# unattended install on it. Demote the RAW below the CDROM so the
# fresh agent ISO is the first fallback after the (blank) disk.
# Restored to 1004 by the final play once the node has joined.
- name: Demote the netboot RAW below the install CDROM (order 1006)
# TrueNAS 25.10 re-validates stored attributes on partial
# updates and rejects a RAW device whose image exists while
# attributes.exists is unset (""Path must not exist..."") —
# resend the attributes with exists=true alongside the order.
- name: Start the VM (retries ride out transient zvol-open error 512)
- name: Approve CSRs and wait for the node to join
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Approve this node's pending CSRs and probe readiness
# Scoped approval only. Kubelet serving CSRs carry the node in
# all arrive as the shared node-bootstrapper SA with no node
# identity in the requestor, so the CSR subject CN inside
# spec.request is decoded and must name this worker — a pending
# CSR from some other joining node is never approved.
$(oc get csr -o go-template='{% raw %}{{range .items}}{{if not .status.conditions}}{{.metadata.name}} {{.spec.username}}{{""\n""}}{{end}}{{end}}{% endraw %}')
- name: Restore the netboot RAW to its steady-state boot order
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Resolve the VM definition for this worker
- name: Restore demoted netboot RAW devices to order 1004
# See the demote task: partial updates must resend RAW
# attributes with exists=true or 25.10 validation rejects.
{{ worker }} rejoined and Ready; netboot RAW restored to its
steady-state boot order. The add-node ISO remains attached but
is NOT a usable reinstall path (its embedded ignition token
expires within ~24h) — rerun this playbook to rebuild again.
Deliberately NOT validated here: storage smoke tests — run one

manually once the democratic-csi driver migration completes.",samples/agreement-pilot/context/V007PILOT-VARIABLE_REFERENCE_REASONING-025.md,negative,not-applicable,yes,no,none,visible-definition,"Script L352-378 defines approve, name, user, subject, n inside the script (L354-361, L373); `{{ worker }}` is Ansible-templated; the go-template braces are in {% raw %} (L368). # reach exporters across VLANs and scrape blackbox on 127.0.0.1.
# daemon.json is intentionally NOT written here. The registry-mirror play in

- name: Deploy prometheus stack docker-compose template
- name: Deploy and verify the prometheus stack

column2: # Smoke-test the netboot.xyz custom binaries by spinning up diskless
# KubeVirt VMs (DHCP from rb5009) for each entry in pxe_test_arches
# and asserting that the matching binary's TFTP hit counter on the
# router increments. Catches regressions in the DHCP -> TFTP path that
# Per-entry fields (see pxe_test_arches below) override the playbook
# defaults, so a single run can mix architectures, firmware modes,
# CUDNs, MACs, and per-VM wait windows.
#   * TFTP hit counter on rb5009 increments for the expected bootstrap
#     iPXE binary (catches DHCP / matcher / TFTP regressions on rb5009).
#   * rb5009 /ip tftp hit counter for the per-host pin filename either
#     increments by 1 (pinned MAC: 'sent') or shows no matching row
#     exists at all (random MAC: 'not_found'). Pin storage lives at
#     {{ netboot_pin_flash_subdir }} on rb5009 flash, registered via
#     assertions on deployed pin bodies catch inventory drift at
#   No per-entry override fields; expectations are fully derived from
#   Namespace selector label is hardcoded to vlan9; testing CUDNs
#     in other VLANs requires the namespace to already carry the
# Namespace handling: the test namespace is ensured (created with the
# vlan9 CUDN selector label if missing) but never deleted -- removing
# CUDN-attached namespaces is currently fragile, and the namespace is
# safe to leave in place between runs. Each VM IS cleaned up via the
# block's always: clause, even on assertion failure.
# Example: two BIOS VMs with pinned MACs, run in parallel
- name: Test netboot.xyz custom binaries via KubeVirt VM PXE boot
# Defaults applied to any pxe_test_arches entry that omits the
# corresponding key. Per-entry fields take precedence.
# Time to wait between VM-Ready and the post-snapshot. SeaBIOS POST
# plus the iPXE ROM's DHCP retry loop can run 60-90s on its own,
# before TFTP even starts; 180s gives margin without dragging the
# When false (default), each entry's create/assert/teardown runs
# serially. When true, all VMs are applied at once, asserted in a
# single pass, then torn down -- noticeably faster for >2 entries
# Default substring to grep for in each smoke pin's served body,
# keyed by lowercase MAC. Drives only the preflight static check;
# per-case substring assertion is dropped because preflight already
# validates the body. Adding a new pinned smoke entry?  Add the
# Each entry must set: arch (free-form label, used in resource
# labels and the default name), binary (TFTP filename to watch on
# rb5009). All other fields are optional overrides:
#                     when multiple entries share an arch)
#   mac               pin the NIC MAC (else KubeVirt generates one)
#   boot_wait_seconds wait between Ready and the post-snapshot
#                     parallel mode the max effective wait wins)
# Default mix: each arch is exercised twice -- once with a
# KubeVirt-generated MAC (random, exercises the un-pinned path
# where the iPXE binary's :tftpmenu MAC lookup misses on rb5009

column2: # What to use for storing Magento media that must be shared across nodes
#   - aws-s3 (default if `aws_use`) - store on AWS S3 media bucket and mount it via the selected S3 backend
#   - aws-efs - store on AWS EFS and mount it as NFS share on the node
#   - local-fs (default if not `aws_use`) - do nothing, just store the files on the local fs
# Note: If you set this to `aws-efs` then the media S3 bucket will not be created, but
# already existing buckets will not be removed.
# Someday: We may want to add plain NFS-based storage in the future to support non-AWS
# use cases or just allow using one of the persistent nodes for shared storage. As EFS is just
# plain NFS under the hood this should be relatively easy as most of the hard work is done.
# How many latest Magento static cache release dirs to keep (must be >=2)
# It weighs nothing so lets protect ourselves in case deploy starts failing

This deliberately does NOT fall back to a built-in address: a committed

# An external runner host is a full FQDN and owns its own DNS elsewhere.
# Technitium API tokens are PER-INSTANCE — one shared token only authenticates the
# node that minted it, so the HA secondaries could not be configured. Log into THIS
# node's API with the shared admin password (technitium_install sets it identically
# on every member) to obtain this node's OWN session token, and use it for every
# API call below. Skipped under technitium_dns_apply=false (molecule/CI, no live API).
# WHY EVERY API TASK IN THIS ROLE IS DELEGATED TO THE CONTROLLER.
# technitium_dns_api_url is http://{{ technitium_dns_host }}:5380 — a NETWORK
# address. Running these tasks on the target meant entering the container over
# pct_remote only to turn around and open a network connection back to that same
# container's own IP. The container is not a privileged vantage point for its own
# API; it is just an extra hop, and it cost one SSH channel PER RECORD. The
# A-record loop alone is ~60 of them, and the paramiko-based pct_remote
# connection reset partway through every time, leaving the zone half-written and
# the run unreachable rather than failed.
# Delegating removes the hop entirely: same URL, same API, same credentials,
# one fewer failure mode. The task still evaluates the INVENTORY host's
# variables, so each member is configured through its own endpoint exactly as
# before — delegation changes where the HTTP call originates, not which host it
# This is NOT the ""delegate_to: localhost tests the controller, not the target""
# anti-pattern. That rule is about PROBES, where the point is to observe from the
# target's own position — and the two wait_for probes in ingress_and_apex.yml are
# deliberately left undelegated for exactly that reason. These are API writes
# whose subject IS the remote endpoint, so the controller is the correct origin.
- name: Authenticate to this node's Technitium API (per-host session token)
- name: Use this node's session token for subsequent API calls

- name: Persist iptables before RKE2 starts programming them

column2: # Reprovision a TrueNAS-hosted VM worker end-to-end, unattended:
#   1. configure_vms.yaml recreates THIS worker's VM with a blank zvol
#      (scoped via truenas_vms_only; other absent VMs are not recreated)
#   2. generate a full add-node ISO (`oc adm node-image create`, no
#   3. copy the ISO to the TrueNAS host, attach/refresh it as the VM's
#      CDROM (order 1005) and demote the netboot RAW below it for the
#      install boot, then start the VM
#   4. approve this node's CSRs (scoped, incl. decoding bootstrapper CSR
#      subjects) until the node is Ready, then restore the netboot RAW
# rebuild) lets this playbook sit in the linear
#   destroy — every play here no-ops (teardown already happened)
#   create  — reconcile: if the worker is already a Ready cluster node
#             the run ends green without touching it; otherwise it is
#             so an existing VM is left untouched either way)
#   rebuild — full reprovision; the node must be absent (asserted)
# E2E tested via AAP 2026-07-31 (3 rebuild cycles).
# Boot design — no netboot-pin changes required: with the zvol blank,
# the install boot falls through disk(1001, blank) -> agent ISO CDROM
# (1005; the netboot RAW is temporarily demoted to 1006 so the install
# never depends on firmware advancing past a failed iPXE exit), RHCOS
# installs and reboots, and the installed disk then boots first forever
# after. After the node joins, the netboot RAW is restored to 1004.
# The stale ISO stays attached but is NOT a usable reinstall path (its
# embedded ignition token expires within ~24h) — to rebuild again,
# - In rebuild mode the node must NOT currently exist in the cluster
# - No CSI smoke test here by design — validate storage manually once
- name: Validate vm_worker_state before touching anything
vm_worker_state must be create, rebuild or destroy
- name: Recreate the VM with a blank zvol (create-only, scoped to this worker)
# Full-ISO mode: suppress the PXE-only bootArtifactsBaseURL field in
- name: End play — vm_worker_state=destroy has nothing to provision
- name: Assert KUBECONFIG is set in the environment
fail_msg: Export KUBECONFIG before running this playbook.
- name: Discover nodes already joined to the cluster

column2: # Chromium itself does not implement the systemd socket-activation protocol (sd_listen_fds() / LISTEN_FDS); it always binds its own --remote-debugging-port. Direct socket activation is therefore not possible, so we deploy a systemd-socket-proxyd in front of Chromium: the .socket unit binds listen_port, the proxy accepts on that activated fd and forwards to backend_port (the port Chromium opens itself). --exit-idle-time on the proxy plus BindsTo= on chromium-headless.service ties Chromium's lifecycle to the proxy, so Chromium stops together with the proxy after the idle timeout.

# Two SELinux booleans are required: bind_any so the .socket can bind the listen port even when it has an unexpected port type (e.g. on Rocky 9, port 9222 maps to hplip_port_t and would otherwise reject the bind); connect_any so the proxy can connect to Chromium's non-standard backend port, which has no matching SELinux port type.
# Run daemon-reload as a regular task (not as a handler), so it runs before the
# state block below and so the restart-socket handler can rely on the registered
- name: 'Flush handlers so that the service is ready for dependent roles'

column2: # Object-storage PITR tier: pgBackRest archives WAL continuously and takes
# scheduled base backups to an S3-compatible endpoint (repo1 = RustFS, and the
# offsite repo2 when enabled — pgBackRest writes both itself; an out-of-band
# mirror used to fill that role and silently copied a truncated subset, #1027).
# Archiving and base backups are primary-only — a standby's WAL arrives via
# streaming, and archive_command runs on the primary. The standby still gets the
# config file, and gives up any backup timer it kept from an earlier primary
# role; see the standby block below. Statically imported from
# main.yml after the cluster is up and the version fact is set, so inner block
# tags (never,pgbackrest_restore) behave exactly like inline tasks.
- name: Configure pgBackRest object-storage PITR backups
- name: Assert the pgBackRest S3 endpoint and credentials are set
pgBackRest is enabled but the S3 endpoint/credentials are unset. Set
- name: Assert the offsite (repo2) endpoint and credentials are set
The offsite repo2 is enabled but its endpoint/credentials are unset.
# A cipher with an empty passphrase is worse than no cipher: pgBackRest
# would refuse at stanza-create, and if it did not, every backup written
# under it would be unrecoverable. Fail here rather than render a config
# that promises encryption it cannot deliver.
- name: Assert a cipher passphrase exists wherever a cipher is enabled
A pgBackRest cipher type is set but its passphrase is empty. Set
POSTGRES_PGBACKREST_REPO2_CIPHER_PASS. Store the passphrase OFF the
guest and confirm it is readable BEFORE the stanza is created — a
passphrase that lives only on the guest makes every backup
unreadable the moment the guest is lost.
- name: Create the pgBackRest config directory
# Async archiving writes its acknowledgement files here (not WAL — the
# background process reads segments from pg_wal directly). pgBackRest does
# not create it, and archive-push fails outright if it is missing.
- name: Create the pgBackRest spool directory
- name: Configure WAL archiving GUCs for pgBackRest
# Reload, not restart: archive_timeout is SIGHUP-settable, unlike
- name: Bound the archive lag on an idle cluster
# archive_mode only takes effect after a restart, and stanza-create/check
# below need archiving live, so flush the restart before touching the repo.
# stanza-create is idempotent and PER-REPO: on an existing host it reports
# ""stanza '<name>' already exists on repo1 and is valid"" (rc=0) while still
# initializing any repo that lacks it. So it runs unconditionally.
# It used to be gated on `pgbackrest info`, which broke two ways. `info`
# reports the stanza as present if it exists in ANY repo, so enabling repo2
# on an existing host skipped creation and left the offsite repo
# uninitialized. And `info` exits 0 with a stub for a missing stanza, so on a
# fresh host the gate never fired at all (#1037).
- name: Create the pgBackRest stanza in every configured repo
# `check` validates archiving against every configured repo, so enabling
# repo2 extends this gate to the offsite copy automatically. Do NOT swap it
# for `pgbackrest verify`: verify exits 0 against a repo it cannot read at
# all, printing only ""No usable backup.info file"" — a wrong-credential
# negative control produced output identical to a real run (#1027).
- name: Verify pgBackRest archiving is healthy
# WAL alone restores nothing — replay needs a base backup to replay ONTO.
# The timers below only schedule one (the first full lands at the next
# Sunday 01:00), so a stanza created on a Monday archives WAL for six days
# while being completely unrestorable. `check` does not catch it: it
# validates archiving, not the presence of a backup.
# `info --output=json` is safe here specifically because stanza-create ran
# first — the ""info stubs a missing stanza"" trap (#1037) needs a stanza that
# was never created. A fresh stanza reports an empty `backup` list.
- name: Check whether the stanza already holds a base backup
# Only ever on an empty stanza, so this is a one-time cost at bring-up, not
# something every converge pays. Expect it to take as long as a full base
- name: Take the initial full backup so PITR has a base to replay onto
# No `first`: info returns a bare [] for a stanza it cannot see, and
# indexing that raises instead of taking the branch. The default('[]')
# keeps check mode (where the command above is skipped and registers no
- name: Deploy the instanced pgBackRest backup service
- name: Deploy a pgBackRest backup timer per schedule
- name: Enable and start each pgBackRest backup timer
# Standby side of the same tier. Only the primary archives WAL and takes base
# backups — a standby's WAL arrives by streaming — but the standby is NOT left
# unmanaged, because two things follow it across a role change and both write to
# The config file: a standby bootstrapped from a base backup inherits the
# primary's archive_command, naming the CLUSTER's stanza. Skipping the standby
# leaves its config file defining some other stanza, so the two disagree until
# the host is promoted — at which point it archives under a name its own config
# does not define. Rendering the same template here makes the file agree with
# the archive_command the host already carries, and makes a promotion continue
# the cluster's existing backup history instead of opening a second stanza.
# The timers: a host demoted from primary to standby keeps whatever backup
# timers it was given, and goes on running base backups against a stanza it no
# longer owns. Nothing else removes them, so this does.
- name: Keep pgBackRest consistent but inert on a standby
- name: Create the pgBackRest config directory
# Discovered rather than derived from postgres_pgbackrest_schedules: the
# schedule list may have changed since this host was a primary, and a timer
# for a since-removed schedule is exactly the one left running.
- name: Find pgBackRest backup timers left over from a primary role
- name: Stop and disable each leftover pgBackRest backup timer
- name: Remove the leftover pgBackRest backup units
# PITR restore (explicit invocation only — the object-storage tier's restore
# drill). Restores the repo into PGDATA and replays WAL to the latest committed
# transaction, or to a pinned target when postgres_pgbackrest_restore_target is
# Point a drill at a scratch cluster/stanza — restoring here overwrites PGDATA.
# Var-gated in addition to the `never` tag: the role include's `postgres` tag is
# inherited here, so a plain `--tags postgres` converge would otherwise select
# it; the postgres_pgbackrest_restore=false default is what keeps it inert.
- name: Stop the cluster before restoring
- name: Restore the repository into PGDATA (delta)
- name: Start the cluster to replay WAL

chore(packer): pin the builder version, and make CI agree with it (#514-adjacent) (#520)
Every template said `required_version = "">= 1.10""`, so any Packer from 1.10
onward could build the guest images and no artifact recorded which one did. The
builder is an input to the image — a different Packer can produce a different
guest — and that is the same defect as the floating
`mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` tag that left the dotnet-analysis image
unbuildable once the tag moved under a reusable cache (#514).
Pinned to `~> 1.16.0` in all six templates: patch releases inside 1.16.x stay
allowed so a security fix is not blocked, and a minor bump becomes a decision
rather than a surprise.
packer/README.md records the exact release, its sha256, and the verify-then-
install steps — a constraint says which versions are ALLOWED, but reproducing an
image needs the one that was USED. Installed as a pinned binary rather than from
HashiCorp's apt repo, which tracks latest and would reintroduce the same drift.
The version I first proposed (1.11.2) was stale; the release index says 1.16.0,
2026-07-24. Checked rather than asserted.
CI ALSO DECLARES A PACKER VERSION, and it said `~1.11`. Raising the templates
without moving CI would have made every `packer validate -syntax-only` fail —
a job that cannot pass is not a check. Two places declaring the same thing with
nothing making them agree is the drift this commit is about, so a test now
asserts the CI version and the template constraint share a series.
Still not pinned, and said so in the README rather than left implicit: `packer
init` fetches the qemu plugin (`~> 1.1`) from GitHub. The `.pkr.hcl.lock` file
it writes is the mechanism that fixes that, and should be committed after the
first init.
Mutations: one template drifting back to `>= 1.10` fails two tests; CI drifting
back to `~1.11` fails a third.

Message-only evidence; first parent not required. Message:
manager: reload the services when an environment file changes
A change to netbox_role_mapping never reached the inventory reconciler on a
production manager. The new value was in
/opt/manager/configuration/inventory-reconciler.env, `osism apply manager`
reported changed=0, and the running container still had the mapping it had been
created with, so the generated inventory kept the old host groups and the
symptom was silent: the reconciler completed and wrote every file.
Only the docker-compose.yml template in service.yml notifies a handler. The
eleven tasks that render an environment file notify nothing, so a change to any
manager environment value is written to disk and never delivered to the
container that reads it. The environment of a container is fixed when it is
created, so a restart cannot pick it up either, the container has to be
recreated.
They now notify ""Ensure that all containers are up"" rather than ""Restart
manager service"". That handler runs
docker compose --project-directory /opt/manager up -d
which is exactly what delivers a new environment, and no more. Measured with
docker 29.7.2 and compose v5.5.0 on a two service project:
* env file changed, then docker restart: same container id, old value
* env file changed, then compose up -d: new container id, new value
* compose up -d with nothing changed: same container id, nothing recreated
* two services, only one env file changed: only that service is recreated
The last two lines are why this handler is the right one. Notifying ""Restart
manager service"" instead would restart the whole manager stack through systemd
and then wait the hardcoded minute of ""Wait for manager service to start"" for
every environment change, even though compose narrows the work to the services
whose environment actually differs.
yamllint with the repository configuration and ansible-lint at the production
profile are clean on roles/manager.
